methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $2.3B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.6B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Divergent, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company founded by Lukas and Kevin Czinger, is currently valued at $2.3B post-money following $600M+ in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 9 private robotics companies at comparable or adjacent stages (Exotec, Locus Robotics, Hadrian, and five others) plus one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.4x multiplier typical of Series E-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $3.2B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Locus Robotics ($2.0B Series F), and Hadrian ($1.6B Series D)—yields a median of $2.0B, establishing a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The two methods diverge materially: stage progression implies growth premium; peer median suggests valuation compression relative to last round.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.7B (floor) to $3.7B (ceiling), with a median of $2.6B. The current $2.3B post-money falls within this band, closer to the peer-median floor. Key uncertainties include the applicability of stage-progression multiples in a capital-constrained environment, the representativeness of the three peer comparables, and whether Divergent commands a valuation premium or discount to peers given unmeasured differences in revenue scale, path to profitability, or technology differentiation.
